causes: old age, in a chair by the fire
a kick from a dray horse
a carriage overturned on the hill
a stroke, at the dinner table
a broken heart, the parish insists
traits: Well thought of in the parish.
Known for a temper, and for apologising.
Remembered at the inn with a toast.
Owed money to several people, and was owed by more.
Wrote long letters to the newspaper.
Known to every child on the street.
Quarrelled with the vicar for thirty years.

virtues.text: Nursed a neighbour's family through the {year} fever.
Gave the winter's coal to the widow next door.
Taught {count} children to read, for nothing.
Pulled a drowning boy from the {town} millrace.
Paid off a dead friend's debts quietly.
Took in an orphaned niece and raised her.
Kept honest weights all their life.
Testified for an innocent man at the assizes.
Shared the harvest in the lean year.
Refused a bribe from the landlord's agent.
Sat with the dying when no one else would.
Forgave a brother who robbed them.
Fed travellers at the back door, no questions.
Gave evidence against a crooked magistrate.

sins.text: Struck an apprentice hard enough to deafen him.
Cheated at cards, often, and well.
Informed on a neighbour for reward.
Turned a pregnant servant out in winter.
Watered the milk for twenty years.
Sold a lame horse as sound.
Left a debt unpaid that ruined a family.
Lied under oath to save a cousin.
Let a rival's barn burn and did not raise the alarm.
Beat a dog to death in a rage.
Abandoned a child to the foundling hospital.
Spread a rumour that drove a woman from {town}.

neutral: Served in the militia; saw nothing.

inflated.title: Fund accounts, {year}
cards: Subscribers: forty townsfolk. Founder's own gift: nothing.
Treasurer's salary drawn: {name_s}, every quarter.
inflated.fact: The relief fund paid its founder a salary; their own gift was nothing.
inflated.q: Tell me about the relief fund.
inflated.a: It was my life's work. Somebody had to manage it.
inflated.conf: Managing it was work. Work is paid. Ask anyone.

inflated.entry: Rebuilt the church roof after the storm.
inflated.title: Vestry minutes, {year}
cards: Roof repairs: paid by public subscription.
Contractor engaged: {name_s}, at double the usual rate.
inflated.fact: The parish paid for the roof, and paid them double to do it.
inflated.a: Every slate. You can still see it from the road.
inflated.conf: Double is what quality costs. The roof did not leak.

inflated.entry: Saved the mill workers' jobs in the slump.
inflated.title: Wage book, {year}
cards: Hands kept on: all. Wages cut: by half.
Owner's dividend that year: the largest ever paid.
inflated.fact: The jobs were kept by halving wages while the dividend grew.
inflated.q: How did you keep the mill open?
inflated.conf: I said everyone sacrificed. I did not say equally.

inflated.entry: Returned a lost purse to its owner, untouched.
inflated.title: Constable's daybook, {year}
cards: Purse returned by {name_s}: empty but for a button.
Owner's complaint: eleven shillings missing. Not pursued.
inflated.fact: The purse came back empty; eleven shillings were never found.
inflated.conf: It was its own reward. Eleven shillings' worth.

hidden_sin.hidden: Poisoned a rival's well during the dry summer.
hidden_sin.title: Coroner's notes, {year}
cards: Three dead at the Hollins farm. Well water: arsenic.
Purchaser of arsenic that month, per the chemist's book: {name_s}.
hidden_sin.fact: They bought the arsenic that killed three at the Hollins farm.
hidden_sin.q: Did you know the Hollins family?
hidden_sin.a: Neighbours. Sad business. The water, they said.
hidden_sin.conf: There was a boundary dispute. There was no longer a boundary dispute.

hidden_sin.hidden: Sold the names of hidden refugees to the soldiers.
hidden_sin.title: Garrison pay ledger, {year}
cards: 'Information received' - paid to {name_s}, twelve crowns.
Same week: nine taken from the {town} cellars.
hidden_sin.fact: They were paid for the names of the nine taken from the cellars.
hidden_sin.q: Where were you the winter the soldiers came?
hidden_sin.a: At home. Keeping my head down, like everyone.
hidden_sin.conf: Twelve crowns fed my family. I did not choose the times.

hidden_sin.hidden: Let an innocent servant hang for their own theft.
hidden_sin.title: Assize record, {year}
cards: Servant girl hanged for theft of plate.
Plate later found pawned. Pawn ticket name: {name_s}.
hidden_sin.fact: The plate a servant hanged for was pawned in their name.
hidden_sin.q: Did you ever lose anything valuable?
hidden_sin.a: Some silver, once. The girl was caught.
hidden_sin.conf: The court decided. I only failed to correct it.

slander.title: Inquest verdict, {year}
cards: Partner's death: accidental, a fall on the ice.
Accusation lodged anonymously, after the verdict.
slander.fact: The 'murder' was ruled an accident; the charge came anonymously, later.
slander.a: He fell. I have told this story so many times.
slander.conf: I did not kill him. I have never once been believed.

slander.entry: Ran a gambling den above the bakery.
slander.title: Magistrate's minute, {year}
cards: Raid on the bakery: nothing found but a prayer meeting.
Complainant: a rival baker. Fined for wasting the court's time.
slander.fact: The 'gambling den' was a prayer meeting; the accuser was fined.
slander.q: What went on above the bakery?
slander.conf: Bad singing is the only sin up there. I admit to the singing.

slander.title: Regimental muster, {year}
cards: Listed deserter in error; was carrying wounded to the rear.
Correction issued, never copied to the civil registry.
slander.fact: Not a deserter: they were carrying the wounded. The correction was never copied.
slander.a: I went. I came back. Not everyone did.
slander.conf: I carried Sergeant Moss two miles. He lived. Ask him.

hidden_virtue.hidden: Hid a family from the soldiers for two winters.
hidden_virtue.title: Letter from a survivor, {year}
cards: 'Two winters in the root cellar of {name_s}.'
'They fed us from their own plate and never told a soul.'
hidden_virtue.fact: They hid a family for two winters and never told anyone.
hidden_virtue.q: What did you do in the war?
hidden_virtue.conf: It was a cellar and some soup. Anyone would have.

hidden_virtue.hidden: Paid a stranger's surgeon's bill anonymously.
hidden_virtue.title: Hospital donations book, {year}
cards: Anonymous: settlement of bed 14's account in full.
Clerk's pencil note: 'it was {name_s}, do not say.'
hidden_virtue.fact: They secretly paid for a stranger's surgery.
hidden_virtue.q: Did you ever help someone you didn't know?
hidden_virtue.conf: Bed fourteen. A boy with a crushed leg. He walked again.

violet.title: Original register, {year}
cards: Original entry for this soul: no charge, no conviction.
Granary fire: struck by lightning, per the fire warden.
violet.fact: The arson entry is a Room 0 amendment; the original register shows nothing.
violet.a: Lightning. Everyone saw it. Why is that on my file?
violet.conf: I never set any fire. Someone wrote that after I died.

violet.entry: Blasphemed before the bishop and was excommunicated.
violet.title: Diocesan register, {year}
cards: No excommunication recorded for this soul.
Margin: last confession heard {year}; absolution given.
violet.fact: The excommunication is a violet-ink forgery; the diocese records absolution.
violet.a: Excommunicated? I took communion every Sunday.
violet.conf: Who wrote that? It isn't true. Who wrote that?

violet.entry: Drowned an infant in the {town} canal.
violet.title: Parish burials, {year}
cards: Infant burial that year: none on this street.
Canal inquest: no body recovered, no case opened.
violet.fact: The infanticide is a Room 0 entry; no child died and no case was ever opened.
violet.a: I fished in it. That's all. I swear that's all.
violet.conf: There was no baby. There was never a baby. Why would anyone write that?

heaven: {name} goes through the Gilt Gate looking back once, as if expecting to be called back.
{name} is received at the Gilt Gate by someone they did not expect.
hell: {name} goes to the Ember Gate. The Wardens enter the debt in red.
{name} is logged in at the Ember Gate. The clerk there does not look up.
